fomc.name: Fed rate decision (FOMC)
fomc.what: The Fed sets the US interest rate 8 times a year (2pm New York), then Powell explains it at 2:30pm.
fomc.cause: The Fed reacts to inflation (CPI/PCE) and jobs (NFP). Markets already guess the decision; the surprise is in the tone and the dot plot.
fomc.gold: Hawkish (more/longer hikes) = dollar and yields up = gold DOWN. Dovish (cuts sooner) = gold UP.
fomc.fx: USD moves most. GBP/JPY usually follows US yields: higher yields weaken the yen, so GBP/JPY up.
fomc.next: Sets the tone for every Fed speaker, the minutes 3 weeks later, and how the next CPI and NFP are read.
fomc.expect: A spike at 2:00pm, often a second move or reversal during the 2:30pm press conference.
fomc.lasts: Days. The biggest scheduled mover for gold (backtest: the first move usually sets the direction into the next day).
fomc.evidence: 16 past releases: gold moved ~$34 in the first hour (5.9x a normal hour; big move 81% vs 25% normally). Same direction a day later 88%. Also moves dollar 6.7x, GBP/JPY 2.5x.
fomc.plan: Be flat or tiny before 2pm. Let the press conference finish, then trade the direction that holds, from your marked zones.

minutes.name: Fed minutes
minutes.what: The written record of the last Fed meeting, released 3 weeks later (2pm New York).
minutes.cause: Shows how many officials leaned toward hikes or cuts, which the statement hides.
minutes.gold: More officials wanting hikes = gold DOWN. More worried about growth or ready to cut = gold UP.
minutes.fx: Mostly a USD event; small knock-on to GBP/JPY via yields.
minutes.next: Feeds rate-bet headlines and Fed speakers over the next days.
minutes.expect: A smaller version of the Fed decision: quick reaction, usually under an hour.
minutes.lasts: Hours; rarely changes the bigger trend (backtest: the first move usually sets the direction into the next day).
minutes.evidence: 16 past releases: gold moved ~$9 in the first hour (1.6x a normal hour; big move 50% vs 25% normally). Same direction a day later 88%. Also moves dollar 1.6x.
minutes.plan: Don't hold a fresh trade into 2pm. Afterwards treat it as a normal session unless gold breaks a key level.

fedchair.name: Powell / Fed speaker
fedchair.what: A Fed official giving a speech or interview.
fedchair.cause: Officials hint at the next move. Powell and voting members matter most; others are background noise.
fedchair.gold: Hawkish words (inflation still too high, more hikes) = gold DOWN. Dovish (worried about jobs, cuts) = gold UP.
fedchair.fx: USD; GBP/JPY only if US yields jump.
fedchair.next: Shifts rate-hike/cut odds, which show up in the next rate-bet headlines.
fedchair.expect: Powell can move gold sharply within minutes. Other speakers usually move it little.
fedchair.lasts: Powell: hours to a day. Others: minutes.
fedchair.evidence: Fed-speaker headlines: no better than a random moment, except Powell himself.
fedchair.plan: Know when Powell speaks (calendar) and avoid entering right before. Ignore most other speakers.

cpi.name: US CPI (inflation)
cpi.what: How fast US consumer prices are rising, monthly at 8:30am New York. Core (no food/energy) matters most.
cpi.cause: Energy, rents, wages and tariffs push prices. The Fed hikes when inflation stays high.
cpi.gold: Hotter than forecast = more hikes = gold DOWN. Cooler than forecast = gold UP. In line = small move.
cpi.fx: USD jumps the most of anything here. GBP/JPY: hot CPI lifts US yields, weakens yen, GBP/JPY slightly up.
cpi.next: Leads to rate-bet headlines, PPI next day, and how the next FOMC is priced.
cpi.expect: The surprise vs forecast decides the size. Gold often whips both ways in the first 15 minutes.
cpi.lasts: Hours to a day (backtest: the first move usually sets the direction into the next day).
cpi.evidence: 23 past releases: gold moved ~$13 in the first hour (1.2x a normal hour; big move 30% vs 21% normally). Same direction a day later 78%. Also moves dollar 2.6x, GBP/JPY 1.4x.
cpi.plan: Write down the forecast before 8:30. Wait for the first 15-min candle to close; trade only if price reaches your zone.

ppi.name: US PPI (producer prices)
ppi.what: Prices businesses pay, monthly at 8:30am New York, usually a day around CPI.
ppi.cause: Raw material, energy and import costs. Rises here tend to reach consumers later.
ppi.gold: Hot PPI = inflation pipeline = gold DOWN. Soft PPI = gold UP.
ppi.next: Economists use it to guess PCE, the Fed's favourite inflation number.
ppi.expect: Smaller than CPI unless it disagrees with CPI.
ppi.lasts: A few hours (backtest: a few hours).
ppi.evidence: 22 past releases: gold moved ~$16 in the first hour (1.4x a normal hour; big move 32% vs 21% normally). Same direction a day later 64%. Also moves dollar 1.8x.
ppi.plan: Treat like a mini-CPI: no entries in the first 15 minutes.

pce.name: US PCE inflation
pce.what: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge, monthly (8:30am New York, often with GDP).
pce.cause: Same drivers as CPI; economists already predict it closely from CPI and PPI.
pce.gold: Hot core PCE = gold DOWN, soft = gold UP, but surprises are usually small.
pce.next: Final inflation input before the next FOMC.
pce.expect: Usually a modest move because it's mostly known in advance.
pce.evidence: 20 past releases: gold moved ~$13 in the first hour (1.2x a normal hour; big move 25% vs 21% normally). Same direction a day later 55%.
pce.plan: Normal caution around 8:30; rarely worth a special trade.

nfp.name: US jobs report (NFP)
nfp.what: Jobs added, unemployment rate and wages. First Friday of the month, 8:30am New York.
nfp.cause: Strong hiring and wages keep inflation up, so the Fed stays tight.
nfp.gold: Strong jobs/wages = gold DOWN. Weak jobs or rising unemployment = gold UP (cuts come closer).
nfp.fx: Big USD move. GBP/JPY moves too: strong US data = yen weaker = GBP/JPY up.
nfp.next: Changes rate odds for the next FOMC; Fed speakers react the next week.
nfp.expect: One of gold's biggest monthly moves; the first spike can whip both ways.
nfp.lasts: 1-2 days (backtest: the first move usually sets the direction into the next day).
nfp.evidence: 20 past releases: gold moved ~$24 in the first hour (2.2x a normal hour; big move 50% vs 21% normally). Same direction a day later 95%. Also moves dollar 3.7x, GBP/JPY 2.4x.
nfp.plan: No positions into 8:30 Friday. Wait 15-30 minutes; the direction that holds often runs into the next day.

claims.name: US weekly jobless claims
claims.what: How many people filed for unemployment last week. Every Thursday 8:30am New York.
claims.cause: Layoffs. A steady rise is an early warning the job market is cracking.
claims.gold: Claims jumping = gold UP. Claims falling = gold slightly DOWN.
claims.next: A run of high claims makes the next NFP look weak in advance.
claims.expect: Usually tiny. Only a big jump (or a trend over weeks) matters.
claims.lasts: Minutes to an hour (backtest: usually fades within the hour).
claims.evidence: 72 past releases: gold moved ~$12 in the first hour (no more than a normal hour; big move 24% vs 21% normally). Same direction a day later 64%.
claims.plan: Mostly ignore; just don't place an entry at exactly 8:30 Thursday.

jolts.name: US job openings (JOLTS)
jolts.what: How many jobs are open in the US, 10am New York, about 2 months old.
jolts.cause: Demand for workers. Fewer openings = cooling job market.
jolts.gold: Falling openings = gold slightly UP; rising = slightly DOWN.
jolts.next: A hint for the NFP later that week.
jolts.expect: Usually no bigger than a normal hour.
jolts.lasts: Under an hour (backtest: usually fades within the hour).
jolts.evidence: 23 past releases: gold moved ~$11 in the first hour (no more than a normal hour; big move 13% vs 22% normally). Same direction a day later 57%. Also moves dollar 1.3x.
jolts.plan: Low priority; trade your normal plan.

gdp.name: US GDP (growth)
gdp.what: How fast the US economy grew last quarter. Advance estimate is the one that moves markets.
gdp.cause: Consumer spending, business investment, trade and government spending.
gdp.gold: Strong growth = USD up = gold DOWN. Weak growth or recession talk = gold UP (safe haven, cuts).
gdp.fx: USD; weak growth tends to strengthen the yen (GBP/JPY down).
gdp.next: Recession worries feed Fed-cut bets and risk-off moves.
gdp.expect: A clear first-hour move, but it often fades by the next day.
gdp.lasts: Hours; often fades next day (backtest: the first spike often reverses within a day).
gdp.evidence: 18 past releases: gold moved ~$19 in the first hour (1.7x a normal hour; big move 50% vs 21% normally). Same direction a day later 44%. Also moves dollar 2.7x, GBP/JPY 1.5x.
gdp.plan: Don't chase the spike; it reverses more often than other releases.

retail.name: US retail sales
retail.what: How much Americans spent in shops last month, 8:30am New York.
retail.cause: Jobs, wages and confidence. Consumers are ~70% of the US economy.
retail.gold: Strong spending = gold DOWN. Weak spending = gold UP.
retail.next: Feeds GDP forecasts and Fed thinking.
retail.expect: A moderate first-hour move; direction often holds into the next day.
retail.lasts: Hours to a day (backtest: the first move usually sets the direction into the next day).
retail.evidence: 12 past releases: gold moved ~$18 in the first hour (1.6x a normal hour; big move 42% vs 21% normally). Same direction a day later 83%.
retail.plan: Wait for the first 15 minutes; trade only at your zones.

ism.name: US ISM business survey
ism.what: Survey of US factory and service managers, 10am New York. Above 50 = growing.
ism.cause: Orders, hiring and prices paid by businesses.
ism.gold: Strong reading = gold slightly DOWN. Weak = slightly UP. The 'prices paid' line matters for inflation.
ism.next: Early read on GDP and jobs.
ism.expect: Usually no bigger than a normal hour for gold.
ism.lasts: Under an hour (backtest: usually fades within the hour).
ism.evidence: 23 past releases: gold moved ~$10 in the first hour (no more than a normal hour; big move 13% vs 22% normally). Same direction a day later 74%. Also moves dollar 1.6x, GBP/JPY 1.5x.

sentiment.name: US consumer sentiment
sentiment.what: Survey of how US households feel and what inflation they expect.
sentiment.gold: Rising inflation expectations = gold DOWN short term (Fed worry), UP longer term (inflation hedge).
sentiment.next: The Fed watches the inflation-expectations line closely.
sentiment.expect: Small move unless inflation expectations jump.
sentiment.evidence: No separate backtest; headline types like this were no better than random.
sentiment.plan: Ignore unless your bias already depends on inflation.

fedbets.name: Rate-hike / cut odds shift
fedbets.what: A report that markets now expect more or fewer Fed hikes/cuts.
fedbets.cause: Usually the result of a data release or a Fed speaker earlier that day.
fedbets.gold: More hikes priced = gold DOWN. More cuts priced = gold UP.
fedbets.fx: USD follows the odds; GBP/JPY via yields.
fedbets.next: Points at the next FOMC meeting; the next CPI/NFP will confirm or reverse it.
fedbets.expect: Mostly explains a move that already happened.
fedbets.lasts: Until the next big data release.
fedbets.evidence: Rate-bet headlines: no better than a random moment (they describe pricing that already moved).
fedbets.plan: Use it to understand today's move, not as an entry signal.

ecb.name: ECB (Europe) decision
ecb.what: Euro-area interest rate decision, 8 times a year.
ecb.gold: Euro is over half of the dollar index: hawkish ECB = euro up = dollar down = gold slightly UP.
ecb.next: Shifts the dollar index for a day or two.
ecb.expect: Indirect and usually small for gold.
ecb.evidence: Not backtested yet: no history of ECB dates in the system.

boe.name: Bank of England decision
boe.what: UK interest rate decision (12pm London), 8 times a year.
boe.fx: Direct hit on GBP: hawkish = GBP up = GBP/JPY UP; dovish or a surprise cut = GBP/JPY DOWN.
boe.next: UK CPI and jobs data get more attention afterwards.
boe.expect: A clear GBP/JPY move, especially if the vote split or guidance surprises.
boe.evidence: Not backtested yet: no history of BoE dates in the system.
boe.plan: For GBP/JPY: be flat into 12pm London; trade the move after the first 15 minutes.

boj.name: Bank of Japan / yen
boj.what: Japan's rate decision (no fixed time, usually Asian morning) or Japan buying yen to support it.
boj.cause: Japanese inflation and a weak yen. Japan has kept rates far below everyone else.
boj.gold: Small: a stronger yen weakens the dollar a little, gold slightly UP.
boj.fx: Huge for GBP/JPY: hawkish BoJ or intervention = yen UP = GBP/JPY DOWN fast, often hundreds of pips.
boj.next: Can unwind 'carry trades' (borrow yen, buy GBP), causing risk-off days.
boj.expect: The most violent event for GBP/JPY. Gold barely reacts.
boj.lasts: Days to weeks if a carry-trade unwind starts.
boj.evidence: Not backtested yet: no history of BoJ dates in the system.
boj.plan: For GBP/JPY: never hold big longs into a BoJ meeting; respect intervention warnings from Japan's finance ministry.

mideast.name: Middle East conflict
mideast.what: War, strikes or threats in the Middle East.
mideast.cause: Fear of a wider war and of oil supply (Strait of Hormuz) being cut.
mideast.gold: Escalation = safe-haven buying, gold UP. Ceasefire or calm = gold gives it back.
mideast.fx: Risk-off: yen up = GBP/JPY DOWN. Oil up.
mideast.next: Oil prices, then inflation worries; weekend news shows up as a Monday gap.
mideast.expect: Fast spike, often faded within a day unless the conflict keeps escalating.
mideast.lasts: Hours to days; fades unless it escalates.
mideast.evidence: Geopolitics headlines: no better than a random moment; the move usually happens before the article.
mideast.plan: Don't chase the spike. Watch for weekend gap risk; reduce size on Fridays when tension is high.

russia.name: Russia / Ukraine
russia.what: Fighting, sanctions or peace talks around the Russia-Ukraine war.
russia.cause: Risk of wider conflict in Europe; sanctions push central banks toward gold.
russia.gold: Escalation = gold UP. Peace talks = gold DOWN a bit.
russia.next: Energy prices in Europe, sanctions news.
russia.expect: Mostly old news by now; only real surprises move gold.
russia.evidence: Geopolitics headlines: no better than a random moment.
russia.plan: Background unless something genuinely new happens.

tariffs.name: Tariffs / trade war
tariffs.what: Import taxes between countries, or talks about them.
tariffs.cause: Politics. Tariffs raise prices and hurt growth at the same time.
tariffs.gold: New tariffs / trade war = uncertainty, gold UP. A trade deal = gold DOWN a bit.
tariffs.fx: Risk-off = yen up, GBP/JPY down. USD can go either way.
tariffs.next: Higher import prices show up in CPI months later; Fed has a harder job.
tariffs.expect: Surprise announcements can move gold $20+; follow-up headlines rarely do.
tariffs.lasts: Days if it is a real new escalation.
tariffs.evidence: Trade headlines: no better than a random moment as a group.
tariffs.plan: Big surprise: wait for the first hour to settle. Follow-up commentary: ignore.

shutdown.name: US government shutdown / debt fight
shutdown.what: US Congress fails to fund the government or argues over the debt limit.
shutdown.gold: Uncertainty and dollar worry = gold UP. A deal = small dip.
shutdown.next: Data releases (CPI, NFP) can be delayed, so the Fed flies blind.
shutdown.expect: Slow, steady support rather than a spike.
shutdown.lasts: As long as the shutdown lasts.
shutdown.plan: Check the calendar: delayed releases can land on unusual dates.

cbgold.name: Central banks buying gold
cbgold.what: Countries (China, India, Poland, Turkey...) adding gold to their reserves.
cbgold.cause: Moving away from the US dollar and sanctions risk.
cbgold.gold: Steady buying = slow support for gold over months. A pause = mild negative.
cbgold.next: Monthly WGC and China reserve data.
cbgold.expect: No quick move. It's why dips get bought, not a trade trigger.
cbgold.evidence: Central-bank gold headlines: no better than a random moment in the hour after.
cbgold.plan: Part of the long-term bullish story; never an entry signal.

etf.name: Gold ETF / fund flows
etf.what: Money going in or out of gold funds.
etf.cause: Western investors reacting to rates and fear.
etf.gold: Inflows support the trend; outflows warn the rally is tiring.
etf.next: Shows up in weekly totals; confirms the trend.
etf.evidence: Fund-flow headlines: no better than a random moment.
etf.plan: Use to confirm the bigger picture only.

cot.name: Positioning (COT report)
cot.what: Weekly CFTC report (Friday) of how big traders are positioned in gold futures.
cot.gold: Extreme net long = crowded, pullback risk. Washed-out longs = room to rally.
cot.fx: Same idea exists for GBP and JPY.
cot.next: Your Sunday review: is the trade crowded?
cot.evidence: Positioning headlines: no better than a random moment.
cot.plan: Only matters at extremes; check it in your weekly routine.

yields.name: US yields / real rates
yields.what: The interest rate on US government bonds. 'Real' yield = after inflation.
yields.cause: Fed expectations, inflation, and government borrowing.
yields.gold: Gold pays no interest, so rising real yields = gold DOWN; falling = gold UP. Gold's main long-term driver.
yields.fx: Rising US yields = USD up, yen down, GBP/JPY up.
yields.next: Follows data and Fed news; drives the bias score on your desk.
yields.expect: Explains moves rather than predicting them.
yields.evidence: Yield headlines: no better than a random moment (they describe the move).
yields.plan: Check the 10-year real yield trend in your bias before each session.

dollar.name: US dollar (DXY)
dollar.what: The dollar's value against major currencies.
dollar.cause: US rates vs other countries, and risk mood.
dollar.gold: Gold is priced in dollars: stronger dollar = gold DOWN, weaker = UP (most of the time).
dollar.next: Shows up in your bias score (DXY 20-day).
dollar.evidence: Dollar headlines: no better than a random moment.
dollar.plan: If gold rises while the dollar also rises, the move has real strength (fear buying).

election.name: Elections / politics
election.what: Political events that could change policy.
election.cause: Uncertainty about taxes, spending, tariffs or Fed independence.
election.gold: More uncertainty = gold UP. Clear result = uncertainty premium comes out.
election.expect: Usually small, except on result day.

physical.name: Asian physical demand
physical.what: Jewellery and bar buying in India and China, and local prices.
physical.gold: Strong demand supports dips slowly; high prices reduce buying.
physical.next: Shows up in import data weeks later.
physical.expect: Doesn't move the world price in the short term.
physical.evidence: Local/physical headlines: below random for moving the global price.

forecast.name: Forecast / opinion
forecast.what: A bank or analyst's view on where gold is going.
forecast.gold: Rarely moves price unless it's a huge bank changing its target.
forecast.plan: Read for learning, not for trades.

price_report.name: Price report
price_report.what: An article saying gold rose or fell.
price_report.cause: It describes a move that already happened.
price_report.next: Look for the real cause: a release, the Fed, or a geopolitical event.
price_report.evidence: Articles that report a move came AFTER the move; gold moved less than normal afterwards.
price_report.plan: Don't trade the headline; check what caused the move.
